memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He slept with Hagar, and she conceived. When she knew she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress. Then Sarai said to Abram, "You are responsible for the wrong I am suffering..." - Gen 16:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The plan worked - Hagar conceived. But instead of bringing joy, it brought a household into ruin. Hagar, now pregnant, despises the barren Sarai. Sarai, stung and bitter, turns on Abram: "You are responsible for the wrong I am suffering." The scheme that was meant to build a family is tearing it apart. Everyone is wounded, everyone is blaming, no one is at peace.

This is what so often happens when we step outside God's will to get what we want. The shortcut delivers the thing - and a whole harvest of misery we never anticipated. Sin frequently gives us exactly what we asked for, along with consequences we never counted on.

Notice the blame flying in every direction. Hagar despises Sarai; Sarai blames Abram; and the plan was Sarai's idea in the first place. When we reap the bitter fruit of our own choices, our instinct is rarely to own it. We look for someone else to hold responsible.

Scripture warns us plainly: "A man reaps what he sows" (Gal 6:7). This isn't said to crush us but to sober us - our choices have consequences, and no amount of blame-shifting removes them. The way forward is not to point fingers but to come honestly before God. When your own plan backfires, resist the urge to blame, and bring the mess to the God who redeems even our failures.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you reaped consequences you didn't anticipate from a shortcut?
- When things go wrong, do you own your part or shift the blame?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when my own plans backfire, keep me from the blame-shifting that only deepens the wound. Help me own my choices honestly and bring the whole mess to You. Thank You that You redeem even my failures.
Amen.
